question.text: What do right-of-way rules decide?

answer.text: Right-of-way rules decide who goes first and who waits when drivers or pedestrians meet where no sign or signal controls traffic.

teaching.text: Where no sign or signal decides, right-of-way rules settle who goes and who waits. Remember: who goes, who waits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Right-of-way rules decide who goes first and who waits when drivers or pedestrians meet where no sign or signal controls traffic.

question.text: Does the law ever grant anyone the right of way?

answer.text: The law only says who must yield; it never grants anyone the right-of-way, not even a driver facing a green light.

teaching.text: The law only tells people when to yield; it never hands anyone the right of way. Remember: law only says who yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The law only says who must yield; it never grants anyone the right-of-way, not even a driver facing a green light.

question.text: Whom must you yield to when approaching an intersection?

answer.text: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers who are already inside an intersection you are approaching.

teaching.text: Pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers already in the intersection go before you. Remember: yield to those already inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers who are already inside an intersection you are approaching.

question.text: Does a green light give you the right of way?

answer.text: A green light lets you go but does not give you the right-of-way; anyone already in the intersection still goes first.

teaching.text: A green light is permission to go, not permission to go first. Remember: green lets you go, not first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green light lets you go but does not give you the right-of-way; anyone already in the intersection still goes first.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: green lets you go, not first

question.text: Who is responsible for avoiding a crash, no matter who has the right of way?

answer.text: No matter who has the right-of-way, every driver is still responsible for avoiding a crash.

teaching.text: Whoever was supposed to yield, every driver must still try to avoid the crash. Remember: everyone avoids crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No matter who has the right-of-way, every driver is still responsible for avoiding a crash.

question.text: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

answer.text: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, who have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk; come to a full stop and let them pass safely.

teaching.text: Stop fully for pedestrians at every intersection and crosswalk and let them pass. Remember: pedestrians always first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, who have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk; come to a full stop and let them pass safely.

question.text: Which pedestrians need extra care, and what should you never assume?

answer.text: Take extra care around children, seniors and people with disabilities, and never assume a pedestrian can see or hear your vehicle or a crossing signal.

teaching.text: Give children, seniors and people with disabilities extra care, and never assume they see or hear you. Remember: never assume they notice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Take extra care around children, seniors and people with disabilities, and never assume a pedestrian can see or hear your vehicle or a crossing signal.

question.text: What usually shows that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind?

answer.text: A white cane or a guide dog is the usual sign that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind.

teaching.text: A white cane or guide dog usually means the pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind. Remember: cane or guide dog.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white cane or a guide dog is the usual sign that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind.

question.text: How is a bicycle treated on the road, and how is a bicyclist treated on a sidewalk?

answer.text: On the road a bicycle counts as a vehicle with many of the rights and duties of a motor vehicle, but a bicyclist on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk has the rights and duties of a pedestrian.

teaching.text: On the road a bicycle is a vehicle; on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk the rider is a pedestrian. Remember: road vehicle, sidewalk pedestrian.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the road a bicycle counts as a vehicle with many of the rights and duties of a motor vehicle, but a bicyclist on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk has the rights and duties of a pedestrian.

question.text: When is a bicyclist treated as a pedestrian instead of a vehicle?

answer.text: A bicyclist on the roadway is treated as a vehicle, but the same rider in a crosswalk or on a sidewalk is treated as a pedestrian.

teaching.text: Where the bicyclist is decides which rules apply. Remember: crosswalk rider is a pedestrian.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A bicyclist on the roadway is treated as a vehicle, but the same rider in a crosswalk or on a sidewalk is treated as a pedestrian.

question.text: Whom must you yield to when merging with or crossing a bike lane to turn?

answer.text: When you merge with or cross a designated bike lane to make a turn, you must yield to bicyclists in that lane.

teaching.text: Yield to bicyclists in a bike lane when you merge with or cross it to turn. Remember: yield to bike lane riders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When you merge with or cross a designated bike lane to make a turn, you must yield to bicyclists in that lane.

question.text: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and what if vehicles arrive together?

answer.text: At a four-way stop the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if vehicles arrive together, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

teaching.text: First to arrive goes first; when two arrive together, the left yields to the right. Remember: first come, then right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a four-way stop the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if vehicles arrive together, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

question.text: At an uncontrolled intersection, who goes first when two vehicles arrive at once?

answer.text: An uncontrolled intersection has no stop signs or lights; when vehicles reach it at the same moment, the vehicle on the left lets the vehicle on the right go first.

teaching.text: With no signs or lights, a tie means the vehicle on the left lets the right go first. Remember: left waits for right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An uncontrolled intersection has no stop signs or lights; when vehicles reach it at the same moment, the vehicle on the left lets the vehicle on the right go first.

question.text: What tie-break do four-way stops and uncontrolled intersections share?

answer.text: Four-way stop and uncontrolled intersection share the same tie-break: when two arrive together, the driver on the left waits for the driver on the right.

teaching.text: Four-way stops and uncontrolled intersections break ties the same way: right goes first. Remember: same tie, right goes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Four-way stop and uncontrolled intersection share the same tie-break: when two arrive together, the driver on the left waits for the driver on the right.

question.text: Whom must you yield to before turning left?

answer.text: Before turning left, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to smaller oncoming road users like bicyclists and motorcyclists, judging their speed and distance carefully.

teaching.text: Before turning left, yield to crosswalk users and to smaller oncoming riders. Remember: walkers and small riders first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before turning left, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to smaller oncoming road users like bicyclists and motorcyclists, judging their speed and distance carefully.

question.text: When does a left-turning driver not have to yield to oncoming traffic?

answer.text: A left-turning driver yields to all oncoming traffic unless holding a green arrow or having arrived first at a four-way stop.

teaching.text: Left turns yield to oncoming traffic unless you hold a green arrow or arrived first at a four-way stop. Remember: left yields unless arrow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A left-turning driver yields to all oncoming traffic unless holding a green arrow or having arrived first at a four-way stop.

question.text: How does a diverging diamond interchange reduce conflicts?

answer.text: A diverging diamond interchange removes the troublesome left-turn movements of a standard interchange, which leaves fewer conflict points with other vehicles.

teaching.text: Removing troublesome left turns leaves a diverging diamond with fewer conflict points. Remember: no troublesome left turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A diverging diamond interchange removes the troublesome left-turn movements of a standard interchange, which leaves fewer conflict points with other vehicles.

question.text: Whom do you yield to when changing lanes or passing?

answer.text: When changing lanes or passing, yield to vehicles already in the lane you want, and do not move over if another driver would have to slow for you.

teaching.text: Yield to vehicles already in the lane, and never move over if someone must slow. Remember: lane owners keep it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When changing lanes or passing, yield to vehicles already in the lane you want, and do not move over if another driver would have to slow for you.

question.text: Whom do you yield to when merging onto a road?

answer.text: When merging, yield to every vehicle on the road you are joining, and do not merge if it would force someone to slow down.

teaching.text: Yield to every vehicle on the road you join, and never force anyone to slow. Remember: merge without forcing slowdowns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When merging, yield to every vehicle on the road you are joining, and do not merge if it would force someone to slow down.

question.text: Whom do you yield to when backing up?

answer.text: When backing up, yield to all vehicles near enough to be a hazard.

teaching.text: When backing, yield to every vehicle near enough to be a hazard. Remember: backing yields to all.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When backing up, yield to all vehicles near enough to be a hazard.

question.text: On a steep road too narrow for two vehicles, which driver normally yields?

answer.text: On a steep road too narrow for two vehicles, the downhill driver yields by backing to a wider spot or stopping to leave room, unless it is more practical for the uphill driver to return to a turnout.

teaching.text: On a narrow steep road, the downhill driver backs up or stops to leave room. Remember: downhill gives way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a steep road too narrow for two vehicles, the downhill driver yields by backing to a wider spot or stopping to leave room, unless it is more practical for the uphill driver to return to a turnout.

question.text: Does the uphill or downhill vehicle normally yield on a narrow mountain road?

answer.text: On a narrow mountain road the downhill vehicle is the one that normally yields, not the uphill one, unless the uphill vehicle can more practically reach a turnout.

teaching.text: The uphill driver yields only when a turnout is more practical for them. Remember: downhill yields, usually.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a narrow mountain road the downhill vehicle is the one that normally yields, not the uphill one, unless the uphill vehicle can more practically reach a turnout.

question.text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with siren or lights?

answer.text: Yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or flashing red, blue, white or yellow lights by pulling to the right edge and stopping where possible.

teaching.text: For sirens, air horns or flashing lights, pull to the right edge and stop. Remember: pull right and stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or flashing red, blue, white or yellow lights by pulling to the right edge and stopping where possible.

question.text: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in an intersection?

answer.text: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside an intersection, continue through the intersection first and then pull over.

teaching.text: If you are inside an intersection, clear it before pulling over. Remember: clear it, then pull over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside an intersection, continue through the intersection first and then pull over.

question.text: How should you pass an emergency vehicle stopped beside the road?

answer.text: Passing an emergency vehicle stopped beside the road, try to leave at least one empty lane between you, or slow to a safe speed and use care if you cannot change lanes.

teaching.text: Leave an empty lane beside a stopped emergency vehicle, or slow down if you cannot. Remember: leave an empty lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing an emergency vehicle stopped beside the road, try to leave at least one empty lane between you, or slow to a safe speed and use care if you cannot change lanes.

question.text: How does your response differ for an approaching versus a stopped emergency vehicle?

answer.text: For an approaching emergency vehicle you pull right and stop, but for one already stopped at the roadside you leave a lane open or slow down as you pass.

teaching.text: Approaching emergency vehicles get a stop; stopped ones get a lane or a slower pass. Remember: approaching stop, stopped move over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For an approaching emergency vehicle you pull right and stop, but for one already stopped at the roadside you leave a lane open or slow down as you pass.

question.text: How much must you slow down passing a stopped emergency vehicle if you cannot change lanes?

answer.text: Unless emergency personnel direct otherwise or conditions prevent a lane change, slow to twenty-five miles per hour when the posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or less, or to twenty miles per hour below the limit when it is above forty-five miles per hour

teaching.text: Slow to twenty-five at limits of forty-five or less, and to twenty under faster limits. Remember: slow down, by the limit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unless emergency personnel direct otherwise or conditions prevent a lane change, slow to twenty-five miles per hour when the posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or less, or to twenty miles per hour below the limit when it is above forty-five miles per hour

question.text: How does the move-over speed depend on the posted limit?

answer.text: Move-over speed depends on the posted limit: at forty-five miles per hour or below slow to twenty-five miles per hour, and above forty-five miles per hour slow to twenty miles per hour under the limit.

teaching.text: Check the posted limit first, then apply the matching move-over speed. Remember: low limit, twenty-five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Move-over speed depends on the posted limit: at forty-five miles per hour or below slow to twenty-five miles per hour, and above forty-five miles per hour slow to twenty miles per hour under the limit.

question.text: How should you treat working service vehicles with flashing yellow and blue lights?

answer.text: Yield to service and maintenance vehicles that are working and showing flashing yellow and blue lights, and take extra care when approaching or passing them.

teaching.text: Yield to working service vehicles with flashing yellow and blue lights and pass with care. Remember: yield to working crews.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to service and maintenance vehicles that are working and showing flashing yellow and blue lights, and take extra care when approaching or passing them.

question.text: How do maintenance vehicle lights differ from emergency vehicle lights?

answer.text: Maintenance vehicles use flashing yellow and blue lights, while emergency vehicles may use red, blue, white or yellow lights with a siren or air horn.

teaching.text: Yellow and blue lights mean a working crew; a siren or air horn means an emergency. Remember: yellow and blue means maintenance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Maintenance vehicles use flashing yellow and blue lights, while emergency vehicles may use red, blue, white or yellow lights with a siren or air horn.

question.text: Why are snow plows dangerous to pass, and what is illegal?

answer.text: Snow plows can be hidden by the blowing snow they throw up, and passing working plows that are staggered diagonally in formation is illegal.

teaching.text: Plows can hide in their own snow, and passing staggered plows is illegal. Remember: never pass staggered plows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Snow plows can be hidden by the blowing snow they throw up, and passing working plows that are staggered diagonally in formation is illegal.

question.text: How should you drive through a work or construction zone?

answer.text: In a work or construction zone, protect crews and other road users by shifting your lane position away from workers and slowing down for obstacles.

teaching.text: In work zones, shift away from workers and slow down for obstacles. Remember: shift away, slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a work or construction zone, protect crews and other road users by shifting your lane position away from workers and slowing down for obstacles.

question.text: How far back must you stop from a school bus with red lights flashing, and for how long?

answer.text: Stop at least twenty feet away from a school bus that has stopped with red lights flashing, and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

teaching.text: Stop at least twenty feet from a school bus with red lights flashing until they stop. Remember: stop twenty feet back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stop at least twenty feet away from a school bus that has stopped with red lights flashing, and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

question.text: Which drivers must stop for a stopped school bus?

answer.text: The school bus stop rule applies on your side of the road, the opposite side or at an intersection ahead, unless a median or other physical barrier separates you from the bus.

teaching.text: Traffic on both sides and at intersections ahead stops unless a physical barrier separates you. Remember: both directions stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The school bus stop rule applies on your side of the road, the opposite side or at an intersection ahead, unless a median or other physical barrier separates you from the bus.

question.text: What is the only thing that excuses you from stopping for a school bus on the other side?

answer.text: The school bus stop applies in both directions; only a median or other physical barrier between you and the bus excuses you from stopping.

teaching.text: Only a median or other physical barrier excuses you from stopping for a school bus. Remember: only a barrier excuses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The school bus stop applies in both directions; only a median or other physical barrier between you and the bus excuses you from stopping.

question.text: What should you do after a school bus turns off its flashing lights?

answer.text: After a school bus turns off its lights, look carefully for children near the bus and crossing the road before you move.

teaching.text: When the lights go off, look for children near the bus and crossing before you move. Remember: look for children first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a school bus turns off its lights, look carefully for children near the bus and crossing the road before you move.

question.text: When must you yield to a transit bus pulling into traffic?

answer.text: Yield to a transit bus that is signaling to pull into a traffic lane when the yield sign on its rear is lit.

teaching.text: Let a transit bus back into traffic when its rear yield sign is lit. Remember: lit yield sign, let it in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to a transit bus that is signaling to pull into a traffic lane when the yield sign on its rear is lit.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: lit yield sign, let it in
